sentence: This project studies how Ebola virus and Marburg virus proteins work with host factors to help the viruses replicate.
This project studies how changes in the extracellular matrix of corneal endothelial cells under stress relate to Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy.
This project tries to find compounds that disrupt the infection process of Gram-negative bacterial pathogens, using infection models.
This project builds predictive models from electronic health records and genomic data to find out how individual patients respond to antidepressants.
This project uses genome and epigenome editing to find out how regulatory elements downstream of the beta-globin locus control the fetal hemoglobin gene.
This project uses single-nucleus methods to study how gene regulation and cell-cell communication drive alcohol-associated liver disease and its recovery.
This project builds and tests facial expression and linguistic measures of negative emotion and social behavior in youth.
This project creates a brain proteomics data set and statistical tools to help researchers study addiction in rat models.
This project tests cervical cancer prevention strategies for women living with HIV.
This project studies how RNA splicing affects colorectal cancer outcomes across patient characteristics, using preclinical models.
This project studies how disrupted alternative polyadenylation relates to differences between patients with myeloid malignancies.
This project builds a bioinformatics resource for generating and analyzing cancer functional proteomic data.
This project compares two intervention skills in self-injuring adolescents and studies how they use and keep those skills in daily life.
This project studies how inhibiting an epigenetic enzyme improves how dendritic cells and T cells work against melanoma.
This project studies where a lipid transfer protein sits at the Golgi apparatus and what it does there.
This project offers imaging equipment, including confocal microscopy and electron microscopy, for vision research.
This project provides liver cell cultures, organoids and organ-on-a-chip models to help study intestinal, liver, and pancreatic diseases.
This project manages and analyzes data from Alzheimer's disease research and develops methods to sort patients into subgroups.
